name: Royal Library
summary: Within Stormwind Keep, scholars turn to the Royal Library for the kingdom’s records and histories. Head Librarian Milton Sheaf watches over its scrolls and treatises, from ancient wars to accounts of realms beyond the sea.

sections.title: A Repository of the Realm
sections.body: Within Stormwind Keep’s guarded halls, the Royal Library offers a quiet place amid courtly intrigue. Milton Sheaf oversees its shelves of southern human history. They hold surviving texts written before the First War, recent military chronicles, and recovered tomes. Alliance scholars, priests, and travelers may browse its treatises on the founding of the Alliance of Lordaeron and the recent arrival of Thrall’s Horde in Kalimdor.

faq.q: Where is the Royal Library located?
faq.answer: The Royal Library lies inside Stormwind Keep, in eastern Stormwind City. From the keep’s grand foyer, follow the corridors to its scholar and archive wings.
Milton Sheaf runs the library as head librarian. He manages its records and helps scholars and adventurers find missing volumes or treatises on the kingdom.

faq.q: What kinds of books can be read here?
faq.answer: Visitors can read histories of the Alliance of Lordaeron, the Guardians of Tirisfal, and the aftermath of the Second War. The shelves also hold reports on the New Horde and regional histories of Stormwind and Alterac.

aliases: who can read in the library
faq.answer: Adventurers of every Alliance race may browse the Royal Library’s collection of scrolls, tomes, and texts on many subjects.

angles.text: As a mage, you can find rare firsthand accounts of Tirisfal’s past, ancient dragon hunts, and the legacy of the Last Guardian.
As an Alliance member, you can read the treaties and war chronicles that bind human, dwarven, and elven peoples through generations of conflict.
